name: Blanket
description:
A tightly woven wool blanket with bound edges, large enough to wrap one adult or add a warm layer to a bedroll. It folds into a flat bundle for tying to a pack.

The blanket offers ordinary comfort and insulation. Severe cold, soaked bedding and exposure remain subject to the GM's judgement; it grants no automatic resistance or resting benefit.

weight.notes: Two pounds for a practical single-person wool blanket, adjusted for ordinary travel rather than a heavy bed covering.

name: Bedroll
description:
A thin padded sleeping mat and light blanket rolled together with two tie cords. The bedroll keeps a traveller off bare ground and provides bedding for an ordinary night under shelter.

The listed weight includes the mat, blanket and cords. A separate blanket may be added for warmth; this purchase includes neither a tent nor weatherproof shelter.

weight.notes: Three pounds for the complete light bedroll; its included blanket and tie cords are already counted.

name: Tent
description:
A low canvas shelter for two Medium travellers lying side by side. Folding poles, wooden pegs and light guy lines are bundled with the tent in a matching wrap. Space inside is modest; bulky baggage may need its own cover.

The purchase includes all listed parts, but no mallet, bedding or climbing rope. Pitching and striking the shelter take practical work and suitable ground; no automatic protection from extreme weather is implied.
saleUnit: One two-person tent with poles, pegs and guy lines

weight.notes: Eight pounds for a compact two-person canvas tent and all included fittings, adjusted from heavier expedition equipment.

name: Bedroll Strap
description:
A broad leather strap with a simple metal buckle, sized to hold a rolled blanket or sleeping mat closed. It can secure a bedroll to suitable loops on a pack.

One strap is supplied. It does not increase the pack's capacity or reduce the weight of anything attached, and it is not a climbing harness.

weight.notes: One tenth of a pound includes the short leather strap and small buckle.

name: Mess Kit
description:
A compact tin pan and shallow plate close around a small cup and spoon, forming one tied bundle. The pan suits warming a simple portion over a modest cooking fire; the other pieces provide basic tableware for one traveller.

All four pieces are included in the listed price and weight. They are represented as one equipment item, without separate nested inventory or extra storage capacity.
saleUnit: One nesting pan, plate, cup and spoon set

weight.notes: Half a pound for a light tin travel set; all four pieces are counted together.

name: Cooking Pot
description:
A small iron pot with a close-fitting lid and swinging bail handle, suited to simmering porridge, stew or water over a hearth. Its broad base is stable on a grate or level stone.

Sold empty. It holds up to 2 quarts of liquid or 4 lb of contents, whichever limit is reached first. Food, water and fuel are separate purchases; add their weight when carried. The lid is not a watertight transport seal.
saleUnit: One empty two-quart iron pot with lid

weight.notes: Three pounds is the empty weight of a small iron pot, lid and handle. Its contents add their own weight.

name: Camp Kettle
description:
A light tinned-metal kettle with a short spout, removable lid and raised carry handle. It is intended for heating drinking water over a small camp fire.

Sold empty. Capacity is 2 quarts or 4 lb of contents. Water and fuel are not included, and the spout prevents the kettle from serving as a sealed travel flask. Add the weight of any water carried inside.
saleUnit: One empty two-quart metal kettle with lid

weight.notes: One and a half pounds for the empty thin-walled kettle, handle and lid; water is counted separately.

name: Cup
description:
A turned wooden drinking cup with a smooth rim and a lightly oiled finish. It is comfortable to hold and durable enough for daily meals or a travelling pack.

Sold empty. It holds up to 1 pint or 1 lb of contents. It has no lid, must be kept upright when filled and should not be placed directly over a fire.

weight.notes: An empty lightweight wooden cup weighs 0.15 lb; any drink adds its own weight.

name: Bowl
description:
A shallow wooden bowl, rubbed smooth and finished with oil, for soup, porridge or a share of the evening stew. Its wide opening makes it easy to eat from and clean.

Sold empty. It holds up to 1 pint or 1 lb of contents. This open bowl has no lid or spill protection and is not intended for cooking directly over a flame.

weight.notes: Quarter-pound empty wooden bowl; food and liquid remain separate carried weight.

name: Spoon
description:
A simple carved wooden spoon with a rounded bowl and a short, smooth handle. It is suitable for eating porridge or stew and stirring a cup of hot drink.

The purchase is one ordinary eating utensil. It is not a full mess kit or a long-handled cooking ladle.

weight.notes: Two hundredths of a pound for a small wooden spoon, retaining a positive weight for large quantities.

name: Wooden Plate
description:
A shallow wooden plate with a raised rim, sized for bread, cheese and a modest meal. Its oiled surface can be wiped clean after use.

The plate is ordinary reusable tableware. It provides no inventory storage capacity, has no lid and is unsuitable for direct cooking over a fire.

weight.notes: Quarter-pound weight for a single practical wooden plate.
